summary: Frontend-only verification of the Coloring canvas bug-fix (single-finger drag must be steady + pinch-to-zoom code path). Tested /coloring/cross and /coloring/sacred-heart in a 390x844 mobile viewport with the session token injected. Result: PASS on all in-scope checks. No React Native red-screen / runtime error from the react-native-gesture-handler + reanimated rewrite. Single-finger mouse drag over the artwork drew a semi-transparent SVG <path> and window scrollY stayed at 0 before AND after the drag (canvas is steady, no scroll/jump). Strokes render on top of the illustration image. Color-palette swatches switch active color, undo removes the last stroke (count 2->1), clear removes all (1->0), reset-zoom button is visible and clickable, share on web triggers the informative alert without crashing. Strokes persist to AsyncStorage across a full page reload (verified on sacred-heart: 1 stroke -> reload -> 1 stroke). Pinch-to-zoom was NOT executed (native multitouch cannot be simulated in the desktop web preview, per the review request); however the Pinch gesture is wired via GestureDetector + Gesture.Simultaneous, MIN_SCALE/MAX_SCALE clamps and focal-point anchoring are present, and the reset-zoom control works without error.
critical_code_review_comments: The Pan/Pinch gestures use Gesture.Simultaneous which is correct so pinch is not blocked by draw, but note that if a user starts a one-finger draw and then adds a second finger, Pan(maxPointers=1) will cancel mid-stroke and Pinch will take over. That is the intended UX and matches the hint text.

content style uses transformOrigin: 'top left' — this is a web CSS property that maps correctly on Expo web; on native iOS/Android it's a no-op but the math (subtracting tx/ty then dividing by scale) already accounts for the top-left origin, so behavior is consistent across platforms.
Minor: onShare uses Alert.alert on web which renders as a browser alert() — verified to not crash. Consider a toast for better UX on web preview but this is out of scope for the bug.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Coloring canvas at /coloring/<slug> uses react-native-gesture-handler GestureDetector with a composed Pan(maxPointers=1)+Pinch gesture inside GestureHandlerRootView. Verified testIDs: coloring-canvas-screen, coloring-canvas, coloring-touch-layer, coloring-reset-zoom, coloring-undo, coloring-clear, coloring-share, coloring-color-<hex> (10 hex values in PALETTE). To reproduce a draw in Playwright: mouse.move to a point inside the coloring-touch-layer box, mouse.down, several stepped mouse.moves, mouse.up — a new SVG <path> appears under the touch-layer SVG. window scrollY stays 0 (canvas is steady). Pinch cannot be simulated in web automation.
rca_of_issue: N/A — bug-fix verification, no new issue found. Prior 'image scrolls while coloring' issue is resolved: because the Pan gesture (with minDistance 0 and maxPointers 1) claims the touch on gesture-handler, the browser's default touch-scroll is suppressed and the artwork stays put during a one-finger drag.
